statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-33845: GnuTLS accepted DTLS handshake fragments with zero length and a non-zero offset, which caused an integer underflow during reassembly and an out-of-bounds read. Upstream advisory GNUTLS-SA-2026-04-29-3 (https://www.gnutls.org/security-new.html#GNUTLS-SA-2026-04-29-3, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/issues/1811) was fixed in GnuTLS 3.8.13 by https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/e5b72c53c7d789d19d1d1cd10b275e87d0415413 ("buffers: switch from end_offset over to frag_length"). Debian fixed it for trixie in gnutls28 3.8.9-3+deb13u4 (DSA-6281-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-33845), which applies the GnuTLS 3.8.13 security patch set to 3.8.9 and carries that upstream commit. The only build of this owner currently published for Debian 13 is made from that Debian version, and the changelog shipped in its libgnutls30t64 package on amd64 and arm64 lists CVE-2026-33845 under 3.8.9-3+deb13u4. The range ends at that build, the lowest published version carrying the fix. Builds made from Debian's earlier 3.8.9-3+deb13u2 and 3.8.9-3+deb13u3 sources predate the fix and sort below it, so they are reported as affected.
